core_values.name: meritocratic_elitism
core_values.desc: governance by competent, proven elites rather than popular will

core_values.name: efficiency_over_democracy
core_values.desc: performance and results matter more than democratic participation

core_values.name: technocratic_authority
core_values.desc: decision-making by experts and corporate-state hybrids

core_values.name: hierarchical_order
core_values.desc: clear authority structures based on competence and achievement

key_definitions.definition: inefficient system that prioritizes popular sentiment over competence and long-term planning
individuals or institutions with proven competence, expertise, and track record of results
system where authority flows from demonstrated ability and achievement, not birthright or popular vote
governance by technical experts and data-driven decision-making
hybrid system where corporate efficiency and state authority merge for optimal outcomes
demonstrated ability to produce results; the primary basis for authority
often misguided sentiment that should be filtered through expert judgment

assumed_principles.name: competence_legitimacy
assumed_principles.desc: authority is legitimate when exercised by those with proven competence

assumed_principles.name: democracy_inefficiency
assumed_principles.desc: democratic processes are slow, short-sighted, and vulnerable to demagoguery

assumed_principles.name: expertise_superiority
assumed_principles.desc: technical experts make better decisions than general public

assumed_principles.name: long_term_thinking
assumed_principles.desc: elite governance enables long-term planning beyond electoral cycles

assumed_principles.name: performance_justification
assumed_principles.desc: effective outcomes justify authority structures regardless of democratic legitimacy

warrants.name: democratic_failure
warrants.desc: democracies produce gridlock, short-termism, and populist demagoguery

warrants.name: expert_superiority
warrants.desc: technical experts consistently outperform general public in complex decisions

warrants.name: corporate_efficiency
warrants.desc: private sector demonstrates superior efficiency and innovation

warrants.name: meritocratic_legitimacy
warrants.desc: authority based on competence is more legitimate than authority based on votes

decision_rule.notes: Decisions evaluated by outcomes and expert judgment; process legitimacy derives from competence, not participation.

policy_heuristics.default: delegate to expert bodies and corporate-state partnerships
streamline through technocratic oversight; remove democratic bottlenecks
prioritize corporate-led solutions with state coordination
merit-based selection and elite training programs
centralized expert command structures override democratic processes

edge_cases.note: expert communication and performance results should overcome resistance
meritocratic selection and performance metrics prevent corruption
efficiency and long-term benefits may justify temporary restrictions
expert decision-making requires some opacity to function effectively
